描述_EN: known as suzhou numerals, they were used by traders to display the price of goods. but, as s. the number '9' is written in black ink, in cursive script, on the sole of the shoe. wells williams notes in the chinese commerical guide (1863), the waves of migration from around china in the 1850s, including guangdong and fujian provinces, where many were facing destitution caused by famine and civil war, had vastly increased the export of neatly crafted straw slippers and other footwear. the upper has a green paper interlining and double ridges to hold its shape. prior to the gold rushes in california in 1849 and australia in 1851, chinese shoes had rarely been exported. in the 19th century, well-to-do men wore backless, square-toed slippers like these tuo xie at home as a type of relaxed footwear during the summer. this pair, made from finely plaited rushes, is decorated with a lozenge pattern in basketweave on the insoles, with leather soles for durability. this type of numerical symbol appeared at the turn of the 20th century. eventually, many chinese settled abroad and engaged in a variety of businesses.
描述_ZN: 被称为苏州数字，它们被商人用来显示货物的价格。 但是，正如S. 数字'9'是用黑色墨水写在鞋底的草书上。 威尔斯-威廉斯在《中国商业指南》（1863年）中指出，19世纪50年代来自中国各地的移民潮，包括广东和福建两省，其中许多人面临着饥荒和内战造成的贫困，这大大增加了整齐的草鞋和其他鞋子的出口。 鞋面有绿色的纸质衬里和双脊来保持其形状。 在1849年加利福尼亚和1851年澳大利亚的淘金热之前，中国的鞋子很少被出口。 在19世纪，富裕的男人在家里穿露背的方头拖鞋，像这样的拖鞋在夏天是一种休闲的鞋类。 这双拖鞋是用细密的芦苇编成的，鞋垫上有菱形图案的花篮，皮鞋底很耐用。 这种类型的数字符号出现在20世纪初。 最终，许多中国人在国外定居并从事各种商业活动。
